The fast-fashion giant plans to complete 20 expansion projects in the U.S. by the end of 2027, including new Zara stores in Denver, Phoenix, and Pittsburgh, as well as expansions of its Massimo Dutti and Bershka brands in New York, along with other store expansions and refurbishments.

second-largest market after Spain. The company has taken a selective approach to expansion, using online orders to gauge demand in individual cities before deciding where to invest in physical stores.

"The U.S., due to the population, and due to the level of relevance, is attracting a lot of interest," Garcia Maceiras said, while stressing that Inditex remains focused on selective and profitable growth.

The retailer has about 2,000 fewer stores than it did in January 2019, reflecting its post-COVID strategy of closing smaller or less productive locations while investing in larger, more efficient stores. While its store count has fallen 27% from its peak, total selling space has declined by only 7%.

As luxury and premium fashion brands raise prices, few middle-income groups are trading down, creating an opportunity for brands like Zara and Massimo Dutti to attract shoppers who still want fashionable products but are less willing to pay luxury prices.

"Many customers are mixing in their wardrobes different types of products from ​different segments of ⁠the market (with) maybe some degree of trading down from luxury," said Garcia Maceiras. "The wardrobe does not belong to one single brand anymore."
